Nisar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 January, 2024
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:8736
Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 13565 of 2023

Applicant :- Nisar
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Applicant :- Umair Mahmood
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Shri Umair Mahmood, learned counsel for the applicant and Shri Rejeev Dhar Dwivedi,
learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No.0074 of 2023, under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 471, 504, 506 IPC, Police Station Nagina, District Bijnor, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that during investigation, earlier applicant was enlarged on anticipatory bail till submission of the Police Report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. on 12.07.2023 vide Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application u/s 438 Cr.P.C. No.7592 of 2023.
4.
He further submits that after investigation, charge-sheet has been filed against him.

He further submits that as applicant was already released on anticipatory bail till submission of the Police Report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C., therefore, he may be enlarged on anticipatory bail till the conclusion of the trial considering the fact that he never misused the liberty of anticipatory bail Nisar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140907998/
1 granted to him and fully co-operated with the investigation.
5.

entities.text: Nisar vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that the applicant is not having any criminal history to his credit.

He placed the reliance upon the observation of the Apex Court made in the case of Md. Asfak Alam vs. State of Jharkhand and another, 2023 8 SCC 632.
6.

entities.text: Md. Asfak Alam vs. State of Jharkhand and another, 2023 8 SCC 632
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail but could not dispute the fact that this Court earlier enlarged the applicant on anticipatory bail in the present matter till submission of the Police Report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. and further could not dispute the fact that applicant is not having any criminal history to his credit.
7.
I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. From the record, it reflects that after lodgement of the FIR, when applicant applied for anticipatory bail application before the court concerned then his anticipatory bail application was dismissed and thereafter he approached this Court during investigation and this Court on 12.07.2023 enlarged him on anticipatory bail till submission of the Police Report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C.

It appears that charge-sheet has been filed against him and there is no allegation that either applicant did not co-operate with the investigation or he misused the liberty of anticipatory bail granted to him during investigation by this Court.

Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the observation of the Apex Court made in the case of Md. Asfak Alam (supra), I am of the view that applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.
9. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

12. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
